notes.title: Bug fixing: Version 1.0.6 is up!
notes.content:
Hello all!

It's been over a month since our previous update, and it's because we have released the Nintendo Switch version in the meantime! Yay! It doesn't mean that we have slacked off on the PC version, but we have had to fix issues on both platforms, so we just packed everything together. Here is the list of fixes brought by this 1.0.6 update:

[list]
[*] Firefly achievement is now fixed;
[*] Fixed issues with minions on level 7, The Forgotten City, and level 9, the Underground Market, that could see Pierre stuck with no possibility to move;
[*] fixed dialogue issues and freezes in some levels.
[/list]

If after updating to version 1.0.6 (version number appears on the lower right corner of your screen when launching the game), you still encounter any of those bugs, please let us know in the comments here or on our [url=https://discord.gg/HD9ZxWy7Ud]Discord[/url]

[h2]Issue Feedback[/h2]
When reporting any issue, please let us know:
[list]
[*] Your system specs (RAM, CPU, GPU, OS + architecture (32 or 64 bits), and any additional information that you think is relevant)
[*] What you were doing when the bug happened (launched a new game, accessing a level already played, etc.)
[*] Any other information that you think is relevant
[/list]

See you soon in Opera City!

notes.title: Ask Us Anything in preparation! Come ask us questions regarding Labyrinth City!
notes.content:
Hi all!

As you all know (and if you don’t, here is a reminder), the PC version of Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective released on June 22, and so far, people seem to enjoy the game tremendously!
As we are preparing for the Switch release in the coming weeks and as we see more and more people attracted by the visuals of the game, its charm, and its beautiful music.

For that reason, we are preparing an AMA — Ask Me Anything. We are not 100% certain on the form this AMA will take, but in any case, we would like to ask you if you have any questions you would like to ask us regarding the game, the work, the studio, the cooperation with IC4Design, our favorite food even! Anything that comes to your mind! We’ll collect the questions and answer the most recurring ones, and we’ll make some time to answer the less recurring as well!

So please fire out, write your questions below, and we’ll do our best to answer them satisfyingly!

notes.title: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective Out Now on Steam!
notes.content:
This is it, folks!

Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is officially out [i]right now[/i], after 3 years of development, hundred of hours poured in making animations, art, dialogues, music, programming, etc.

We hope you'll enjoy following Pierre and Carmen's adventures throughout Opera City.
We hope you'll love getting lost in the different mazes, by yourself or with your loved ones.
We hope you'll find all the hidden objects, treasures and references.

But, most of all, we hope you'll have an amazing time playing Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective!

Here is our official trailer to celebrate the release!

[previewyoutube=fXz1xidDWW8;full][/previewyoutube]

And remember, Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is:

[list]
[*] 10 levels adapted from the original double-page spread illustrations from IC4Design
[*] Over 100 hidden objects
[*] Over 500 interactions
[*] MILLIONS of lines of dialogues (okay, maybe not *millions*, but a good amount nonetheless)
[*] Hours of fun
[/list]

See you soon in Opera City!

notes.title: Labyrinth City in Digital Dragons’ Indie Celebration - Demo incoming!
notes.content:
Hello! Long time no see!

Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is proud to announce that it has been chosen among 250 entries to appear alongside 60 other titles as finalist for Digital Dragons’ 2021 Indie Celebration on May 13 and 14! As part of the event, we are releasing a 2-level demo for the game (and this time, we mean it) on Steam for a limited time, so call in sick tomorrow, because there are mazes that need to be trodden, hidden objects to be found, and magic stones to be retrieved.

We hope you will enjoy this demo. We have improved the game in many subtle ways these past months compared to the preview of February, but we have also improved the game in not-so-subtle ways, adding a TON of dialogue lines, interactions, sound effects, and more. 

Get your magnifying glasses and put on your deer caps, detectives, Opera City needs you!

Note: Mr X has stolen the "Exit" button on the home screen, thinking it would prevent people from enjoying the game. Should you find yourself in a situation where you need to exit the game, the recommended course of action is to not exit the game but to physically exit from your computer’s vicinity. Alternatively, you can alt+F4. The choice is yours

notes.title: Labyrinth City off of Steam Winter Game Festival & Minigame
notes.content:
Hello,

As you are all aware, Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective was set to participate in the Steam Winter Game Festival that takes place from Feb 3 to Feb 9. As the PC release of the game will be available exclusively on Steam, at least at first, we consider it an important event and we were very excited to present our demo to you all.

Unfortunately, for reasons beyond our control, we have had to pull out of the festival. We feel terrible as we worked very hard to propose a demo that, we hoped, would be appealing to all and representative of the final game, to give players a good idea of what to expect. To celebrate this event, we had planned to unveil our store page in other languages, two of which (Russian and Korean) had never been announced before, and we also put together a new trailer for Steam.

After discussion, we have decided to turn this step-back into something that could be, we hope, a fun experience and a good way for you to discover the different voices of Labyrinth City: We have created a (small) Internet Maze. At the end of your journey lies the accursed demo, will you be brave enough to fight your way through our social media cringe and reach your destination?

If so, click on one of the five images below to start your journey!

notes.title: The Mr X who stole Christm... the magic stone!
notes.content:
It was a day like any other day in Opera City,
But somebody was staring at a stone with envy.
An ancient stone famous for its density,
Its density, its rarity and its magic ability.

Mr X, our eccentric yet malevolent malefactor,
made his way through the streets and to the museum.
Circumventing the master in his domain: the director,
Mr X moved with marvelous momentum.

Stepping on the pedestal, in a flutter of his cape,
He snatched the stone and slipped out, unflustered.
Stealing with his prize behind a drape,
He escaped! But see: its power is unfettered.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38763391/6dc3bd4e1256c33595e2ca62416bb48c081d39ae.png[/img]


[i]Happy holidays to you all![/i]

Yay!

notes.title: What is Labyrinth City?
notes.content:
We are pouring our hearts and souls in the making of Labyrinth City, a game that we have a real attachment to since Noam, digital producer of Darjeeling, chanced upon a certain book by IC4DESIGN while browsing the alleys of a Parisian bookshop with his children. A book that should not have been picked up by the family, as Noam’s significant other owns a bookshop of her own. A book called Pierre The Maze Detective. If that is not fate speaking, what is? After that little trip, Noam knew immediately that he would make a game from this, and here we are!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38763391/ada60f7bf4d5f3a77996bec4ee4397e65333bcb4.png[/img]

So, how does one turn a book into a game? Well, in that case, the first step was to contact IC4DESIGN, the original creator of Pierre The Maze Detective, and enquire whether they would be interested in seeing their beloved creation take life in a game that would allow players of all ages to wander through the intricate and detailed world they designed as Pierre. Upon receiving the request, the Hiroshima-based design studio was thrilled and eager to cooperate to make the game unique in every possible way, to the point that not only did they rework Pierre’s face for the benefit of the game! In that respect, the game is a real tribute to a work of art that well deserves its international reputation.

Next order of business was to animate everything. The studio has painstakingly given life to many, many, MANY characters and objects in the game, with which players can interact, to lend a sense of motion to each scene and have them enjoy exploring and talking to the different characters. You will be amazed at how much animation and narration has gone into the game. You will get caught up in trying to reach that chest hidden somewhere in the winding platforms of the forest level or in finding every star around the docks. You will soon find that running after Mr X is simply an excuse to visit marvelous scenes and places.

To make sure that each visit to Opera City is as interesting as the first, our studio has implemented a few minigames (that might or might not remind you of your childhood) here and there within the incredible visuals of Labyrinth City ([i]but ssssh, it’s a secret still[/i]).

As we are fond of the game and the universe created by IC4DESIGN, we want to make sure players enjoy the experience and come back to the game in order to explore every nook and cranny in each level, so replay value was something that was considered from the beginning. After all, the original book is a detective book, and what does a detective do if not look for things and people? As such, not only will you be able to search for a TON of hidden objects and missions.

Last, but certainly not least, the game will benefit from an original soundtrack that will give it a life of its own and will make the overall experience a delight for your visual and auditory appendages!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38763391/c9231eab4096c021744ab65216f42092525a0ec7.png[/img]

We hope you enjoyed reading this little bit of information about the game, head over to our [url=https://twitter.com/city_labyrinth]social media platforms[/url] to keep in touch with any news related to the game!

notes.title: indiePlay 2020 - Labyrinth City nominated in the Best Overseas Game category
notes.content:
Hello all, and welcome!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38763391/2cabdda7e6a6aa3dc20718fd8b2f30ccf7b35e4b.png[/img]

We hope you are as eager as us to see Labyrinth City being launched in 2021, but first, we would like to share some good news: Labyrinth City has been nominated in the [url=http://www.indieplay.cn/blog/2020-indieplay-11-15-weplay]Best Overseas Game[/url] category of indiePlay 2020. Held annually since 2015, [url=http://www.indieplay.cn/]indiePlay[/url] has grown to be the biggest and most respected indie game award in China. We are very happy and humbled to have been chosen alongside talentuous studios and amazing games. The winners of each category will be announced on November, 15th during the WePlay conference so, win or lose, expect an update from us at that time!

Stay tuned for more information!
